docs.title: Switchyard Protocols
docs.text:
Mechanics of Libsy follows the work exchanged through run_stream. This section explains the data inside that work: an LLM conversation or a set of typed questions for a decision model.

Both use provider-neutral Rust types from the switchyard-protocol crate. These types define Switchyard's protocols. Your application converts its inputs into these types, passes them to libsy, and converts model calls and responses at its provider boundary.

docs.title: Why use a neutral protocol?
docs.text:
Provider APIs describe the same interactions in different ways. An Anthropic tool call is a tool_use content block. OpenAI Responses uses a function_call item. Chat Completions puts it in an assistant message's tool_calls array.

An algorithm needs to know that the model called a tool, its name, and its arguments. A shared ToolCall gives it those facts without tying the algorithm to one provider's JSON. Your gateway or agent harness keeps control of the client, credentials, and execution.

Application or provider data
          |
       convert
          v
Switchyard protocol types <--> libsy algorithm
          |
       convert
          v
Your model client and provider API

The protocol crate defines the data exchanged with libsy. Conversion and network calls happen in your application or in optional Switchyard crates. When handling run_stream, your application can use any client and return the protocol response through CallModel::respond or CallDecision::respond. The crate also provides optional client traits that help Switchyard's supplied clients and execution helpers work together.

docs.title: Two kinds of model interaction
docs.text:
Interaction Protocol fields and types Used when Read next LLM conversation Request.llm_request: LlmRequest; Response.llm_response: LlmResponse Your application starts a run or serves Step::CallModel. Content can include text, tools, reasoning, and media. LLM-Related Protocols Typed decision CallDecision.request: DecisionRequest; the work future returns libsy::Result<DecisionResponse> Your application serves Step::CallDecision. Named questions ask for a Boolean estimate, a choice, or a rubric score. Decision Model-Related Protocols

The LLM envelopes also carry metadata: Option<Metadata>. That application metadata is separate from the provider's conversation content. Decision calls use their own request and response types directly.

docs.title: Choose who owns conversion
docs.text:
Integration choice Use it for Your own adapters Convert an existing SDK's types or an in-process model's data to and from switchyard-protocol. Keep your existing client and transport. switchyard-translation Decode and encode supported LLM JSON and streaming events while keeping your own transport. switchyard-llm-client Use Switchyard's HTTP clients, including LLM translation and typed decision adapters.

The two guide pages explain these boundaries and the integration flow. For field-level details, use the LLM request reference or decision question reference. Each reference page links back to its guide and to the next part of the exchange. For complete type and method definitions, open the protocol crate reference.

docs.title: Decision Model-Related Protocols
docs.text:
A decision model evaluates a context against named questions and returns typed answers. An algorithm can use those answers to choose a model or decide what work to request next.

Switchyard represents this exchange with DecisionRequest and DecisionResponse. These are the types exchanged through Step::CallDecision.

System One is a common API for open decision models, including Jev. Switchyard supports it alongside OpenAI Decisions through the same protocol.

Question fields, answer types, and API mappings

  • Question reference: shared context, question IDs, Boolean/choice/score questions, and provider request mappings.
  • Answer reference: probabilities, rubric scores, confidence, usage, provider response mappings, and errors.

docs.title: Describe the questions
docs.text:
One request carries shared context and independent questions keyed by ID. Each DecisionQuestion defines what to evaluate and which answer kind to return. The response uses the same question IDs, so the algorithm can match each answer to its question.

Here is a request asking whether a task contains private information. This is request construction only; it does not call a provider.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use serde_json::json;
use switchyard_protocol::{DecisionKind, DecisionQuestion, DecisionRequest};

let request = DecisionRequest {
    model: Some("privacy-judge".into()),
    context: json!({"task": "Summarize this customer's account history."}),
    questions: BTreeMap::from([(
        "contains_private_data".into(),
        DecisionQuestion {
            instructions: json!("Does the task contain private customer data?"),
            kind: DecisionKind::Boolean {
                true_description: Some(json!("Contains private customer data")),
                false_description: Some(json!("Contains only public information")),
            },
        },
    )]),
};

For required option IDs, rubric levels, and validation responsibilities, see question construction and validation.

docs.title: Interpret the answers
docs.text:
DecisionResponse::answers maps the same question IDs to DecisionAnswer values. Each answer separates its typed value from optional provider_confidence. For the privacy question, ProbabilityTrue(Probability(0.8)) means an estimated 0.8 probability that the answer is true. It is not a routing choice until the algorithm applies its policy. Choice questions can name any supported set of candidates; their shape is not limited to two models.

The answer value reference explains rubric scores, distributions, and the difference between a Boolean judgment and an answer probability.

docs.title: Understand conversion
docs.text:
For supported questions and answers, conversion is a direct, lossless mapping of decision data. IDs, answer probabilities, rubric positions, and confidence retain their meanings. Structured values become JSON text where OpenAI requires strings. This retains their content, rather than making the two wire formats identical or providing an arbitrary JSON round-trip guarantee.

Both adapters return probabilities for Boolean answers. A custom backend that returns only true or false can use BooleanEstimate::Value without inventing certainty. Optional distributions remain None when absent. The OpenAI adapter reports refusals as errors because DecisionValue has no refusal variant.

docs.title: Own the conversion
docs.text:
When handling Step::CallDecision, use your existing client or a function to convert call.request into the backend's format, send it, and convert the answer into DecisionResponse. Pass that work to call.respond as a future returning libsy::Result<DecisionResponse>.

Match question IDs and kinds, and retain available distributions and confidence separately. The question reference links the System One and OpenAI adapter implementations. Decision conversions live in switchyard-llm-client; switchyard-translation handles LLM formats.

RoutedDecisionClient is an optional interface that lets Switchyard's clients and execution helpers work together. Direct run_stream handling does not require implementing it. See Mechanics of Libsy for the call-handling loop and cancellation behavior.

docs.title: Use the supplied clients
docs.text:
You can instead use the public SystemOneClient or OpenAiDecisionClient from switchyard-llm-client. Use dependencies at the same API revision as libsy and the protocol crate.

This async excerpt sends the earlier request to System One. Set its model to an ID served by your endpoint. SYSTEM_ONE_ENDPOINT must include /v1/systemone. Running it makes a provider call and may incur a charge. The trait import makes the supplied client's call method available; you do not implement a client in this example.

use std::time::Duration;
use switchyard_llm_client::SystemOneClient;
use switchyard_protocol::RoutedDecisionClient;

let client = SystemOneClient::new(
    std::env::var("SYSTEM_ONE_ENDPOINT")?.parse()?,
    std::env::var("SYSTEM_ONE_API_KEY")?,
    Duration::from_secs(30),
)?;
let response = client.call(request).await?;

OpenAiDecisionClient::new takes the same arguments, with an endpoint ending in /v1/decisions and that provider's key. Each adapter makes one attempt per call; its timeout covers the request and reading the response body.

For the built-in execution path, register decision clients by model ID with ClientRouter::single_with_decision_clients or new_with_decision_clients, then use switchyard_llm_client::run. The algorithm still receives the same typed DecisionResponse whichever client performs the call.

docs.title: LLM-Related Protocols
docs.text:
An LLM request describes a conversation, the tools available to the model, and generation settings. Switchyard represents these in LlmRequest. The same type works whether the next call goes to Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, or Chat Completions.

Fields, API mappings, and conversion rules

  • Request reference: messages, tools, generation settings, and their provider API fields.
  • Response and stream reference: output content, token usage, event types, and stream lifetime.
  • Translation reference: engine methods, preservation policies, diagnostics, and edits before encoding.

docs.title: Read a request
docs.text:
LlmRequest separates instructions from conversation turns. A Message contains a role and ordered ContentBlock values. Content can include text, media, reasoning, tool calls, and tool results.

This example constructs the neutral request passed to an algorithm. It uses the quickstart's dependencies.

use switchyard_protocol::{ContentBlock, InstructionBlock, LlmRequest, Message, Request, Role};

let request = Request {
    llm_request: LlmRequest {
        instructions: vec![InstructionBlock {
            role: Role::System,
            content: vec![ContentBlock::Text { text: "Answer briefly.".into() }],
        }],
        messages: vec![Message::text(Role::User, "Explain tail latency.")],
        ..LlmRequest::default()
    },
    ..Request::default()
};

Request is the host-facing envelope. It adds optional correlation metadata and raw_request, a host-owned JSON body. Codecs use LlmRequest::preservation for replay, not Request::raw_request.

docs.title: Read a response
docs.text:
The host returns a Response envelope containing LlmResponse. LlmResponse::Agg holds a completed AggLlmResponse. LlmResponse::Stream holds a single-consumption stream of LlmResponseStreamEvent values. Each stream event exposes neutral chunks through normalized(). Chunks describe message starts, text deltas, tool arguments, usage, and completion. An event may also retain parsed provider JSON for same-format replay.

Usage::input_tokens counts non-cached input. The codecs separate cache-read and cache-write tokens from OpenAI's aggregate input counts. Missing counts stay None. Call LlmResponse::into_agg().await when you need a buffered result; this consumes the stream and aggregates its normalized chunks.

docs.title: Understand lossless conversion
docs.text:
The protocol retains source data for lossless same-format round trips. With the default preservation policy, decoding a supported API body and encoding it back to that API reuses its preserved JSON. The preservation reference explains exactly what is retained and when replay takes precedence.

Conversion between different provider APIs can be lossy. For example, Anthropic has no separate developer role, and Chat Completions has no native equivalent for every Responses built-in tool. Keeping the original data in the protocol does not give the destination API those capabilities.

Translation reports known losses in diagnostics. The translation policy reference explains how to allow or reject these conversions.

Encoding an edited request

A preserved same-format body takes precedence over normalized fields. If you change the protocol fields and want those edits encoded, remove that format's entry from preservation.requests, or encode with PreservationPolicy::Disabled. The same rule applies to preservation.responses for buffered responses.

See stream preservation and aggregation for how replay and edits work on streamed responses.

docs.title: Use the translation crate
docs.text:
switchyard-translation supplies the LLM codecs without making network calls. Add it at the same API revision as libsy and switchyard-protocol, following the quickstart's translation setup.

This excerpt decodes an inbound Chat Completions body and encodes it as an OpenAI Responses request. It can run inside your adapter; outbound.body is the JSON your client sends.

use serde_json::json;
use switchyard_translation::{TranslationEngine, TranslationPolicy, WireFormat};

let engine = TranslationEngine::default();
let policy = TranslationPolicy::default();
let inbound = json!({
    "model": "your-model",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain tail latency."}]
});

let decoded = engine.decode_request(WireFormat::OpenAiChat, &inbound, &policy)?;
let outbound = engine.encode_request(
    WireFormat::OpenAiResponses,
    &decoded.request,
    &policy,
)?;
// Check diagnostics from both operations before sending the encoded body.

During a libsy run, place decoded.request in Request::llm_request. Encode the request from Step::CallModel for the selected backend. Decode its reply with decode_response, or use decode_stream_event and encode_stream_event with a separate StreamTranslationState per response stream. Return the neutral Response through the call object, as shown in Mechanics of Libsy.

The engine also exposes translate_request and translate_response for direct API-to-API conversion. See the translation engine reference for signatures and results.

docs.title: Keep your own client or conversions
docs.text:
You can construct these protocol types from your existing SDK and convert them back yourself. When handling Step::CallModel, pass call.respond a future that uses your client and returns libsy::Result<Response>. Keep content order, tool IDs, provider-only data, and streaming lifetime intact where your integration needs them.

RoutedLlmClient is an optional shared interface used by Switchyard's clients and execution helpers. Direct run_stream handling works with your own functions or clients; it does not require implementing that trait.

If you want Switchyard to handle HTTP and translation, use TranslatingLlmClient from the HTTP client crate. The quickstart shows how to keep your own HTTP client. Typed decisions use the separate contract described in Decision Model-Related Protocols.

docs.title: Interactive coding agents with single-provider auth
docs.text:
Route Codex or Claude Code between models from one provider using your saved CLI login. Every target, including the classifier, must use that provider.

These composite routing recipes use a classifier to choose the starting tier for each user turn. Stage adjusts routing during tool calls. forward_auth passes your login through to the models.

Choose one recipe. Each uses local port 4123.

docs.title: Codex with OpenAI
docs.text:
Sign in with codex login. Terra classifies, and Stage routes between Sol and Luna.

This recipe needs Codex classifier support added after v0.3.0. Install from a checkout of current main:

cargo install --locked --path crates/switchyard-server

Save as codex-routing.toml:

schema_version = 1

[llm_clients.chatgpt_backend]
format = "openai_responses"
base_url = "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"
forward_auth = true

[targets.capable]
id = "gpt-6-sol"
llm_client = "chatgpt_backend"

[targets.efficient]
id = "gpt-6-luna"
llm_client = "chatgpt_backend"
extra_body = { store = false, stream = true }
omit_body_fields = ["max_output_tokens"]

[targets.terra]
id = "gpt-6-luna"
llm_client = "chatgpt_backend"
extra_body = { store = false, stream = true }
omit_body_fields = ["max_output_tokens"]

[routes.switchyard]
id = "switchyard"
type = "composite"

[routes.switchyard.classifier]
target = "terra"
base_threshold = 0.5
classify_trigger = "user_turn"

[routes.switchyard.stage]
capable_target = "capable"
efficient_target = "efficient"
confidence_threshold = 0.5

Start the server:

switchyard-server --config codex-routing.toml --dry-run
switchyard-server --config codex-routing.toml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4123

Create ~/.codex/switchyard.config.toml (or place it beside your config.toml if you use a custom Codex config directory):

model = "switchyard"
model_provider = "switchyard"

[model_providers.switchyard]
name = "Switchyard"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4123/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true

In another terminal, launch Codex:

codex --profile switchyard

docs.title: Check the routing
docs.text:
Send a prompt, then check which models handled the answer and classification:

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4123/v1/stats \
  | jq '{answers: .models, classifier: .classifier.models}'

docs.title: API and Model Compatibility
docs.text: Check three things separately: the protocol format, the model's capabilities, and the integration executing the algorithm. Supporting an API format does not guarantee that a model supports every feature represented by that format.

docs.title: Supported API formats
docs.text:
These are the supplied adapter paths. Applications embedding libsy may own their conversions instead. See Switchyard Protocols for the neutral types and integration flow.

API Supplied support Read the exact contract OpenAI Chat Completions LLM request, buffered response, and streaming conversion; optional HTTP client. Requests, responses OpenAI Responses LLM request, buffered response, and streaming conversion; optional HTTP client. Requests, responses Anthropic Messages LLM request, buffered response, and streaming conversion; optional HTTP client. Requests, responses System One Typed Boolean, choice, and score questions through the supplied decision client. Used by open decision models, including Jev. Questions, answers OpenAI Decisions Typed decision questions through the supplied decision client. Questions, answers

Provider fields have different equivalents and limitations across APIs. Preservation supports lossless same-format replay. Cross-format conversion may lose information. See translation policies and preservation before relying on a particular feature.

docs.title: Model requirements
docs.text:
Libsy algorithms select from the model IDs supplied by the host. There is no fixed model-name allowlist in the routing core. Your endpoint and credentials must serve the IDs you configure.

Model role Check before use Guidance Answer model Context length, tool calling, input modalities, and requested output format for the actual workload. Model checks LLM judge Structured output matching the algorithm's verdict schema and sufficient output budget. Judge compatibility Decision model Served question kinds and response fields matching the configured adapter. Decision protocol guide Local or trained router The trained assets and backend expected by that algorithm. Prefill routing

The measured model pairs and benchmark configurations are examples with recorded workloads and settings. They are not an exhaustive supported-model catalog. Recheck capability and availability on the endpoint you will actually use.

docs.title: Integration restrictions
docs.text:
Integration Configuration owner Important boundary Hosted OpenRouter router OpenRouter request controls. Only provider-exposed algorithms and settings apply; runner TOML is not its API. NeMo Relay Switchyard runner configuration inside Relay. Check Relay version and plugin credential rules. LiteLLM LiteLLM inventory and plugin configuration. The experimental decision-only integration cannot serve intermediate model calls. Direct libsy Your application. Your host must fulfill every requested call and handle the final outcome. Local reference server Runner TOML and local server settings. Demo and personal use, not a supported production deployment.

For dependency revisions, follow the quickstart or the selected integration's instructions. Development callback examples use a different API from the released 0.3.0 bindings and crates.

docs.title: Host Integration
docs.text:
Add libsy where your gateway or agent harness chooses and calls a model. Your application keeps its transport, credentials, and lifecycle.

Start with the Rust quickstart for a working example. Use Mechanics of Libsy for execution and Switchyard Protocols for data conversion. This page covers the responsibilities specific to your host.

docs.title: Choose the integration boundary
docs.text: Host Insert routing here Preserve from the existing application Gateway After request admission and input decoding, before model dispatch. Authentication, tenant isolation, budgets, model inventory, provider credentials, and response delivery. Agent harness Before each model turn, after assembling conversation and tool history. Tool execution, task state, model clients, conversation storage, and the agent loop.

docs.title: Host responsibilities
docs.text:
Dispatch every requested call. Apply your credentials, budgets, and access policy to routing-time judge calls as well as answer calls. Send internal calls through model dispatch without entering the same router again. Supply only models your host can reach. See call handling and final-outcome handling.

Keep history and state. Supply the tool history required by the algorithm; provider continuation IDs alone can hide that evidence. Scope session IDs to the tenant and conversation. Reuse algorithm instances when they retain session decisions, and decide how your host handles concurrent turns and multiple processes. State behavior is algorithm-specific; see Composite sessions and the Plan/Execute history requirement.

Observe the complete run. Include judge calls and final model work in your host's observations. Configure telemetry collection in your application and instrument model I/O performed by your own clients. See the OpenTelemetry reference.

For existing integrations, check NeMo Relay or the LiteLLM compatibility notes. The experimental LiteLLM plugin supports decision-only routing and cannot serve intermediate model calls.

docs.title: Serve routing-time calls
docs.text:
Use your existing client as shown in the Step loop. The shared client traits below are optional.

Optional: adapt the shared client traits

docs.title: Development API
docs.text:
These adapters use the quickstart's development dependencies. Their asynchronous reply method differs from the synchronous callback API in the released v0.3.0 crates.

When using RoutedLlmClient or RoutedDecisionClient, adapt errors to LibsyError:

use switchyard_libsy::{CallDecision, CallModel, LibsyError, Result};
use switchyard_protocol::{RoutedDecisionClient, RoutedLlmClient};

async fn serve(call: CallModel, client: &dyn RoutedLlmClient) -> Result<()> {
    let request = call.request.clone();
    let model = call.models[0].clone();
    call.respond(async move {
        client.call(request).await.map_err(|error| LibsyError::client_call(model, error))
    }).await
}

async fn serve_decision(call: CallDecision, client: &dyn RoutedDecisionClient) -> Result<()> {
    let request = call.request.clone();
    let model = call.model.clone();
    call.respond(async move {
        client.call(request).await.map_err(|error| LibsyError::client_call(model, error))
    }).await
}

docs.title: Python bindings
docs.text:
The bindings run the same Rust algorithms. The local routing example below works with the released package. For the asynchronous callbacks and cleanup described after it, build matching development bindings and follow the complete Python host example.

Python setup, callbacks, and metadata

With Python 3.10+ and uv, create a project and install the released package:

uv init --bare switchyard-python-demo
cd switchyard-python-demo
uv add "nemo-switchyard==0.3.0"

Save as route.py:

import asyncio
from switchyard.libsy import Step, algorithms

async def main():
    router = algorithms.stage_router(
        picker="efficient_first", confidence_threshold=0.5)
    models = {"efficient": ["Efficient"], "capable": ["Capable"]}
    models["any"] = ["Efficient", "Capable"]
    text = {"type": "text", "text": "Hello"}
    request = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [text]}]}
    async for step in router.run_stream(request, models):
        if isinstance(step, Step.Done):
            print("Selected:", step.outcome.selected_model_ids[0])

asyncio.run(main())

uv run route.py prints Selected: Efficient without making a network call.

docs.title: Concurrent calls and cancellation
docs.text:
The client coroutine returns LlmResponse.Agg or LlmResponse.Stream. Pass the coroutine itself to respond:

await call.respond(client.call(call.request, call.models[0]))

respond cancels and awaits the supplied provider work before returning. For concurrent algorithms, create handler tasks and cancel and await the remaining handlers when the run ends, as in the Python host example. Awaiting one handler at a time serializes execution. call.fail(error) is also awaitable; decision calls use the same reply pattern.

For the shared cancellation behavior and upstream limits, see Mechanics.

docs.title: Metadata and telemetry
docs.text: After checking that outcome.metadata is present, read its outcome_id, algorithm, and evidence attributes. Evidence is a normal Python value, usually a dictionary; algorithms without evidence return None. See the OpenTelemetry reference for signals and export setup.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text: Reference for the spans, attributes, and metrics emitted by libsy and its LLM client.

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text: Your application installs a tracing-opentelemetry subscriber and global OTel meter provider, and owns exporters, filtering, sampling, context propagation, and flushing. Libsy installs none of these and sends no telemetry itself. Environment variables alone do not enable collection. See OTel Rust setup and OTLP configuration.

docs.title: Spans and attributes
docs.text:
Span Emitted by Meaning libsy.run Libsy One algorithm run, including routing-time work. OpenInference kind CHAIN. libsy.llm_call Libsy driver Waiting for the host to fulfill an offloaded call. Includes host queueing. OpenInference kind CHAIN. libsy.decision_call Libsy driver An offloaded Decision Model call, including host queueing. OpenInference kind CHAIN. libsy.client_call, exported as chat <model_id> LLM client driver One candidate model call, including that candidate's retries. OTel kind CLIENT; OpenInference kind LLM.

Hosts driving run_stream without the LLM client driver instrument their own model I/O.

libsy.decision_call records algorithm, selected_model, and terminal outcome. Successful replies add available input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, reasoning_tokens, gen_ai.response.id, and gen_ai.response.model fields. Unknown values are omitted; request content, answers, and error details are not recorded.

docs.title: Routing outcome fields
docs.text:
On libsy.run:

Attribute Type Meaning / presence algorithm, switchyard.algorithm string Name from Algorithm::name(). switchyard.route string Inbound request model/route, when present. outcome string ok or error when the algorithm task resolves. outcome_id string Successful outcome's ID. OutcomeMetadata::new generates a UUIDv7. selected_model_ids string array Successful outcome's selected model followed by ordered fallbacks. This is a plan, not proof that every model was called. session_id, session.id string Request session ID, when supplied. Both names carry the same value. agent_id, task_id, task_kind, agent_role, correlation_id string Corresponding request metadata, when supplied. evidence.source, evidence.verdict, evidence.trigger, evidence.reason_code string Known string fields from outcome evidence, when present. evidence.score, evidence.confidence, evidence.threshold number Known numeric fields from outcome evidence, when present.

RoutingOutcome.metadata is available in Rust and Python. Its optional JSON evidence exports only the listed keys with matching types; unknown keys and wrong types are omitted. Evidence may be absent. Scores and confidence have algorithm-specific meanings. Failed runs return typed errors, not outcome metadata; successful fail-open decisions may carry a fixed reason_code.

docs.title: Model-call fields
docs.text:
The LLM client driver records these on libsy.client_call:

Attribute Type Meaning / presence algorithm, switchyard.algorithm, selected_model string Algorithm and candidate model ID. switchyard.candidate, switchyard.candidate_count integer One-based candidate position and number of candidates. gen_ai.operation.name string chat. gen_ai.request.model string Requested model; the translating client records the upstream model name. gen_ai.request.stream boolean Recorded as true for streaming requests; otherwise omitted. gen_ai.request.temperature, gen_ai.request.top_p number Sampling values represented in the request IR, when set. gen_ai.request.top_k, gen_ai.request.max_tokens integer Sampling/output limits, when set. gen_ai.request.reasoning.level, gen_ai.output.type string Reasoning effort and recognized output type (text or json), when set. gen_ai.conversation.id string Request session ID, when supplied. server.address, server.port string, integer Upstream host and port, recorded by the translating client. gen_ai.response.id, gen_ai.response.model string Values supplied by the upstream response. gen_ai.response.finish_reasons string array Available normalized stop reasons. gen_ai.usage.input_tokens integer Input tokens including cache reads and cache creation. gen_ai.usage.output_tokens integer Output tokens. gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens integer Cache-read and cache-creation input tokens. gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens integer Reasoning output tokens. outcome string ok, error, or cancelled. error.type, error string Failure category/status and error description on this client span.

gen_ai.provider.name is intentionally unset: an endpoint or model name does not reliably identify the provider. Usage fields are omitted when unavailable, not invented as zero. Available counts are capped at OTel's signed integer maximum.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metrics use the switchyard meter scope. The tables use OTel instrument names.

docs.title: Routing and client metrics
docs.text:
Instrument Type Labels Meaning switchyard.runs Counter algorithm, outcome Completed algorithm tasks, including failures. switchyard.run_duration_ms Histogram algorithm, outcome Algorithm-task duration in milliseconds. switchyard.algorithms_in_flight UpDownCounter algorithm Active algorithm tasks; exported as a Prometheus gauge. switchyard.decisions Counter algorithm, selected_model Published routing decisions. switchyard.llm_calls Counter algorithm, selected_model, outcome Routing-time LLM calls and each terminal answer candidate, including failures. switchyard.llm_call_duration_ms Histogram algorithm, selected_model, outcome One duration sample in milliseconds per offloaded LLM call or terminal answer candidate, including failures; see streaming limits below. switchyard.decision_calls Counter algorithm, selected_model, outcome Offloaded Decision Model calls, recorded once on reply, failure, or unfulfilled drop. switchyard.decision_call_duration_ms Histogram algorithm, selected_model, outcome One duration sample in milliseconds per Decision Model call, including host queueing. switchyard.total_requests ObservableGauge none Process-wide total of successful and failed answer candidates after routing, including reused routing responses. switchyard.total_errors ObservableGauge none Process-wide total of failures after routing, including failed answer candidates and reused routing responses. switchyard.requests Counter model Successful answer candidates or reused routing responses, by model ID. switchyard.errors Counter model Failed answer candidates or reused routing responses, by model ID. switchyard.model_call_latency_ms Histogram model Successful answer-candidate duration in milliseconds, including that candidate's retries and stream consumption. Excludes routing time and reused routing responses. switchyard.routing_overhead_ms Histogram algorithm LLM client driver's time to obtain a successful routing outcome, including judge calls but excluding any subsequent answer call. switchyard.classifier_fail_open Counter judge_model, reason Judge failures that caused classification to proceed without a verdict. switchyard.upstream_attempts Counter outcome, code HTTP attempts, including retries, made by the translating client. switchyard.router_retry_recovered Counter none Upstream operations that succeeded after a retry.

Algorithm/call outcome is ok or error. HTTP attempt outcome is ok for 2xx, retryable_error for 408/429/5xx or failures without a status, and other_error otherwise. code is an allowlisted status, a status-class bucket, or none. Classifier reason is timeout, transport, upstream_5xx, upstream_non_5xx, invalid_response, parse_error, client_error, or call_error.

Client requests, routing decisions, model calls, and HTTP attempts have separate counts. For switchyard.llm_calls and switchyard.llm_call_duration_ms, each routing-time offloaded call and each terminal answer candidate contributes one observation. HTTP retries stay within the same candidate's count and duration. Reusing a response produced during routing keeps only its routing-time call observation.

For example, one buffered client request with no judge calls or retries, a failed primary, and a successful fallback produces one client response, one routing decision, two llm_calls, and two llm_call_duration_ms samples. The primary has selected_model=<primary> and outcome=error; the fallback has selected_model=<fallback> and outcome=ok. For terminal answer-candidate observations, selected_model identifies the model called. For routing-time observations, it identifies the initial routing candidate. For switchyard.decisions, it identifies the initial routing selection.

The five request/error/latency instruments above record each answer candidate after routing, not each HTTP attempt. A failed candidate followed by a successful fallback adds two to total_requests, one to total_errors, one to errors for the failed model, and one to requests for the successful model. Routing-time calls and failures before a routing outcome do not contribute. A response reused from routing contributes one to total_requests and one to either requests or errors (also total_errors on failure), but no model_call_latency_ms sample. The model label is the candidate's configured model ID (the serving model for a reused response). For terminal answer candidates, it matches selected_model on llm_calls and llm_call_duration_ms. The two total gauges are cumulative process-wide compatibility values.

For streams, these five instruments record when the response stream ends or is dropped. Stream errors count as failures. Dropping an unfinished stream also counts as a failure; a terminal message permits a successful drop. Failed calls have no model_call_latency_ms sample.

docs.title: Algorithm-specific metrics
docs.text:
Stage Router instruments use the prefix switchyard.stage_router.:

Suffix Type Labels Meaning routing_decisions Counter decision_source, target_name Choices by decision source and semantic target name. probability Histogram none Scorer's capable-model probability. confidence Histogram none Confidence used to resolve or defer a turn. severity Histogram none Tool-failure severity. spinning Histogram none Repeated unproductive tool activity. exploring Histogram none Exploratory tool activity. production_intensity Histogram none Production-oriented tool activity.

These histograms contain unitless values from 0 to 1. They are recorded when tool signals reach the scorer, including when it defers to a classifier. They are not one sample per application request and are not split by route or session.

Advisor Gate instruments use the prefix switchyard.advisor_gate.:

Suffix Type Labels Meaning reviews Counter verdict, trigger Review outcomes and what triggered them. consult_failures Counter reason Failed advisor consultations. discarded_turns Counter none Executor turns discarded after a redo verdict. discarded_tokens Counter kind Tokens in discarded turns; kind is input, cached, cache_creation, or output.

docs.title: Timing and streaming
docs.text:
• libsy.run may finish before the answer call. Nested algorithms have separate run spans.
  • Decision calls record error when failed or dropped without a reply, including cancellation. Cancelled calls do not poll further host work. A response completed during a cancellation race may still record its result. These metrics work with any host and do not require a client observer.
  • libsy.llm_call and routing-time call metrics end when the host fulfills the offloaded call. They include host queueing. The LLM client driver buffers routing streams before fulfilling the call. The span's input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, and reasoning_tokens fields are buffered-response only.
  • For terminal answer candidates, switchyard.llm_calls and switchyard.llm_call_duration_ms record when the response stream ends or is dropped. Duration includes that candidate's retries and stream consumption. Stream errors and unfinished drops record outcome=error; a terminal message permits a successful drop.
  • libsy.client_call remains open while its stream is consumed. IDs, usage, and finish reasons update from normalized events. An unfinished stream dropped by its consumer records cancelled; a stream error records error.

docs.title: Data exposure
docs.text:
Built-in evidence excludes prompts, responses, and raw errors. Custom evidence is checked for field names and types, not string contents or lengths. Client spans may include error descriptions and upstream addresses; algorithm logs may include content such as Advisor Gate's reply_head. Supplied session/correlation IDs are included. Review collected data before exporting it outside your deployment.

Custom algorithms can record OTel instruments directly. Keep metric labels to configured names and fixed categories, not request/session IDs or user text.

docs.title: Source and stability
docs.text:
These are current implementation names, not a separately versioned telemetry schema. Debug spans and log events are not a stable field contract.

  • Libsy spans, outcome projection, and metrics
  • Client span fields and stream/usage observation
  • Client metrics
  • Stage Router metrics and Advisor Gate metrics

Use the Rust quickstart for compatible dependency versions. Mechanics of Libsy explains how these crates work together during a run.

docs.title: TOML Schema
docs.text:
The native deployment file defines the LLM clients, targets, and routes that a Switchyard server serves. It is read by switchyard-server --config.

Validate a file without starting the server:

switchyard-server --config routes.toml --dry-run

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
schema_version = 1

[llm_clients.openrouter]
format = "openai_chat"
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
api_key_env = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"

[targets.strong]
id = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5"
llm_client = "openrouter"

[routes.default]
id = "switchyard"
type = "passthrough"
target = "strong"

schema_version must be 1. Table names under llm_clients, targets, and routes are local references; clients send the route's id as the model name.

The optional top-level fallback_client names an entry under [llm_clients]. When set, any HTTP method and path not implemented by Switchyard is forwarded through that client without translating the path, query string, body, response, or model identifier. The fallback client does not need a target. Only its base_url is used: caller end-to-end headers are forwarded, hop-by-hop headers are removed, and configured API keys, extra headers, format, and retries are not applied. When omitted, unmatched paths return 404.

schema_version, [targets], and [routes] must all be present, even when a route reaches no upstream. A file without a [targets] table is rejected with missing field targets; an empty [targets] table satisfies it. [llm_clients] defaults to empty and may be omitted.

docs.title: [llm_clients.<name>]
docs.text:
Key Required Default Meaning format Yes — openai_chat, openai_responses, or anthropic_messages. base_url Yes — Upstream base URL. context_discovery No unset Set to "llama_cpp" to enable /props context discovery for VGR efficient targets. Disabled when unset. An explicit route context_window takes precedence. api_key_env No unset Name of the environment variable holding the key. Omit to send no authentication. forward_auth No false Forward the caller's provider credential and application headers. A route's forwarding clients must use one credential family unless they all use the same scheme, host, and port, such as one LLM gateway. extra_headers No {} Custom HTTP headers sent to the model server. Set credentials with api_key_env or forward_auth; the server rejects headers owned by the selected auth mode. Header names are case-insensitive. responses_reasoning No "preserve_encrypted" Responses reasoning replay: "preserve_encrypted" or "drop". Only valid for openai_responses. fallback_on_rate_limit No true Try another completion candidate after an upstream HTTP 429 exhausts retries. Set to false to return the 429 instead. max_retries No 2 Retry budget, 0–10. failure_cooldown_ms No 5000 (5 seconds) Skip a backend for this many milliseconds after an exhausted transient completion failure. Zero disables it. timeout_ms No unset Deadline in milliseconds for all attempts, retry delays, and the complete response, including stream reads. Must be at least 1. Unset leaves the wait unbounded.

For openai_responses, responses_reasoning controls replay of reasoning history. Every client defaults to "preserve_encrypted": reasoning items with non-empty encrypted_content or a stored reasoning id are retained with empty content. ID-only reasoning is removed when the request sets store: false. Switchyard's translated Anthropic reasoning is always removed. Reasoning without either is removed. Set responses_reasoning = "drop" explicitly for a backend that cannot consume provider reasoning. Both modes keep messages, tool calls and tool results. The setting is rejected on other client formats, even when no target uses the client. It is not inferred from the model name or URL.

The TOML never contains the secret itself. api_key_env names a variable that must exist and be non-empty when the server loads.

Cooldown is enabled by default for 5 seconds. Set failure_cooldown_ms = 0 to disable it. The cooldown starts after retries are exhausted.

failure_cooldown_ms tracks transport failures, timeouts, HTTP 408/429, and 5xx responses after retries. State is shared across callers per model within the client, including callers using forwarded credentials. With forward_auth = true, HTTP 429 triggers request-local retries and, by default, fallback; other callers keep trying the model. For shared credentials, HTTP 429 also triggers cooldown by default. During cooldown, ordered fallback tries the next candidate. A terminal cooldown error returns HTTP 503. Calls resume together after expiry. Auxiliary calls and errors after a stream is returned leave cooldown state unchanged.

With fallback_on_rate_limit = false, HTTP 429 does not start cooldown, so later requests can receive the upstream response too. Retry budgets and deadlines still apply. Other errors keep their existing fallback and cooldown behavior. This option controls completion candidates; judge and advisor error recovery is unchanged.

timeout_ms applies separately to every call through the client, including judge verdicts and answers. To give a judge a short deadline without limiting the answering models, put the judge on its own [llm_clients] entry; two entries may share a base_url. When an answer deadline expires, the server returns 504. If the final answer has already started streaming, the server sends a framed error and ends the stream without a success marker.

The Rust runner collects streams used during routing before the algorithm continues, preserving provider events for replay. After the configured retries, an HTTP client failure stops routing unless the call enables recovery. Capability classifiers and advisor gates default to fail_open = true. A capability classifier routes to the capable tier on judge failures, including deadlines. An advisor returns the buffered executor turn when its consult fails. Set fail_open = false to stop the request on these failures. Answer calls keep their usual error behavior.

Set forward_auth = true to use each caller's credential instead of a server-owned key:

[llm_clients.claude]
format = "anthropic_messages"
base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
forward_auth = true

forward_auth cannot be combined with api_key_env. OpenAI clients forward authorization, chatgpt-account-id, and x-openai-fedramp. Anthropic clients forward authorization or x-api-key; for Claude subscription OAuth, they also forward oauth-* values from anthropic-beta and remove all other inbound beta values.

This setting gives base_url the caller's login. Enable it only when that upstream should receive the credential, and use HTTPS unless the upstream runs on loopback. Other application headers are preserved and may contain provider-specific credentials. Forwarding clients do not follow HTTP redirects.

A forwarded credential belongs to the service that issued it. A ChatGPT login, for example, must never reach Anthropic. So all forwarding clients in a route, including classifier and judge targets, must use one credential family: OpenAI (openai_chat and openai_responses clients, which serve Chat Completions and Responses callers) or Anthropic (anthropic_messages clients, which serve Messages callers).

The exception is one host that serves both formats, such as an LLM gateway that accepts each caller's gateway key on its OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints. A route may mix the two families when all of its forwarding clients use the same scheme, host, and port in base_url; the path may differ:

[llm_clients.gateway_responses]
format = "openai_responses"
base_url = "https://gateway.example.com/v1"
forward_auth = true

[llm_clients.gateway_messages]
format = "anthropic_messages"
base_url = "https://gateway.example.com"
forward_auth = true

Such a route serves Chat Completions and Responses callers and forwards the caller's bearer token to every forwarding client. The server returns 400 without calling an upstream when a caller uses an API that the route does not serve.

These limits apply only to forwarded credentials. A client with api_key_env sends the server's own key, so a route can mix formats and providers through such clients.

docs.title: [targets.<name>]
docs.text:
Key Required Default Meaning id Yes — Exact model ID sent upstream. llm_client Yes — Key under [llm_clients]. system_prompt No unset System prompt prepended when this target serves a completion. extra_body No {} Values merged into the upstream request when the request does not already set that key. omit_body_fields No [] Top-level fields removed from every request body that Switchyard sends to this target. Switchyard removes them after it translates the request to the LLM client's format, so use that format's field names, for example reasoning_effort on openai_chat or reasoning on openai_responses. Switchyard applies extra_body and reasoning_effort after the removal, so either can set a removed field again. reasoning_effort No unset Reasoning effort forced on every request to this target, replacing the value the caller sent (reasoning.effort on openai_responses, reasoning_effort on openai_chat). Rejected on anthropic_messages clients. Use it to run one target at a different effort than the client asked for, for example a strong tier at max behind a client that sends high. Targets with different effort settings need distinct model IDs when used within one route. Separate routes may use the same model ID with separate llm_clients entries (same endpoint, different name).

Within one route, callable targets with the same model ID must use the same llm_client. This includes completion targets and targets used for judging or classification. Switchyard rejects same-model targets on different clients within a route because execution is keyed by model ID. Separate routes may use the same model ID on different clients.

Each selected or fallback target is prepared from the routed request independently. A prompt configured for one target is therefore not carried into another target's fallback request. Judge-only, classifier-only, and reviewer-only targets are not completion destinations and do not receive this prompt.

Escalation's weak target and Advisor's executor produce a candidate response while routing, so their target prompt is applied to that call. A prompted target in either role cannot use the same model ID as that route's judge or reviewer because those calls would otherwise be indistinguishable at the client boundary; Switchyard rejects that configuration when it loads. Token-count requests do not apply target system prompts.

docs.title: [decision_clients.<name>]
docs.text:
Decision clients serve typed judgments for routing classifiers.

Key Required Meaning format Yes system_one or openai_decisions. endpoint Yes Full API URL, including the endpoint path. api_key_env Yes Environment variable holding a non-empty API key. timeout_ms Yes Request and response deadline in milliseconds; must be at least 1.

For OpenAI Decisions:

[decision_clients.decisions]
format = "openai_decisions"
endpoint = "https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions"
api_key_env = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
timeout_ms = 5000

[decision_targets.judge]
id = "gpt-6-luna"
decision_client = "decisions"

Each decision_targets entry pairs an upstream model id with a decision_client. OpenAI receives structured context, instructions, and descriptions as JSON text.

docs.title: [routes.<name>]
docs.text:
Every route takes the common keys below, plus the keys for its type.

Key Required Default Meaning id Yes — Public model ID that callers send in requests. type Yes — Routing algorithm for this route. context_window No unset Positive token count that GET /v1/models advertises for this route as data[].context_length. Unset values appear as null. This does not enforce a request limit. tool_calling No unset Tool-calling support advertised by GET /v1/models. When false, the server rejects tool definitions, tool controls, and tool history with HTTP 400 before dispatch. Unset values appear as null. Explicit true and unset values do not restrict requests. reasoning No unset When false, the server rejects reasoning controls with HTTP 400 before dispatch. Explicit true and unset values do not restrict requests. The server does not include this declaration in GET /v1/models. vision No unset Image-input support advertised in GET /v1/models under data[].capabilities.vision. When false, the server rejects images with HTTP 400 before dispatch, including images in tool results. Unset values appear as null. Explicit true and unset values do not restrict requests. Declare true only when every target the route can select accepts images.

docs.title: Optional infrastructure check
docs.text:
A capability llm_classifier route without escalation may include [routes.<name>.infra]. Both tiers must have one model; each model may have multiple workers. A host applies the policy explicitly with Route::apply_infra after Route::decide, using periodically collected model-pool metrics and local in-flight counts. Plain decide and execute retain task routing. Sub-agent routing is unchanged.

[routes.example.infra]
max_signal_age_ms = 3000
min_waiting_requests = 4
max_capable_inflight = 2

All keys are required. Limits must be positive. Missing or stale observations retain the task decision. See the Dynamo PreProc example for collection and capacity safeguards.

docs.title: noop
docs.text:
Returns a buffered assistant response containing OK without calling an upstream model. Use it for local smoke tests.

A noop-only deployment reaches no upstream but still needs the [targets] table, which can be empty:

schema_version = 1

[targets]

[routes.smoke]
id = "noop-route"
type = "noop"

docs.title: passthrough
docs.text:
Sends parent requests to one target. It can also route delegated sub-agent work; see Sub-Agent-Aware Routing.

Key Required Meaning target Yes Target used for parent and harness-maintenance requests. subagents No Nested passthrough or llm_classifier policy used only for delegated sub-agent work. Nested classifiers currently support only mode = "custom".

docs.title: random
docs.text:
Splits traffic across targets. See Random Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning targets Yes — Target names to choose from. weights No equal Finite, non-negative relative weights in targets order, with at least one positive value. Invalid weights are rejected at load time. seed No unset Reproduces the selection sequence.

docs.title: plan_execute
docs.text:
Plans on a capable target, then switches to an efficient target after the first recognized edit or write tool call. See Plan/Execute Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning capable_target Yes - Target used for read-only inspection and planning. efficient_target Yes - Target used after the first edit or write. tool_semantics.mutate No [] Additional tool names that trigger handoff. See the example. planning_prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the planning instruction. handoff_prompt No unset Adds an instruction to the handoff request. planner_reasoning_as_text No false Converts visible planner reasoning summaries to assistant text at handoff.

docs.title: prefill_router
docs.text:
Experimental in v0.3.0

Switchyard v0.3.0 does not provide or support a router checkpoint, an exporter, or compatible encoder assets. You must obtain or train a compatible checkpoint and obtain its encoder and tokenizer yourself. There is no supported end-to-end checkpoint export and compatibility contract. The example below shows configuration syntax, not a ready-to-run deployment.

Routes the latest non-empty user message with a checkpoint-backed prefill classifier. Build switchyard-server with --features prefill-router and make the prefill router's Python dependencies available in the active virtual environment.

Key Required Default Meaning targets Yes — Target names in the exact order expected by the checkpoint outputs. checkpoint Yes — Path to the tensor-only router checkpoint. Relative paths use the server's working directory. device No auto PyTorch device used for encoder inference, such as cpu, cuda, or cuda:0. cache_dir No unset Directory where Hugging Face caches the downloaded encoder and tokenizer. max_length No 2048 Maximum tokenized encoder input length; longer prompts are truncated. batch_size No 32 Maximum prompts per encoder forward pass. 
[routes.prefill]
id = "switchyard/prefill"
type = "prefill_router"
targets = ["fast", "strong"]
checkpoint = "/models/router.pt"

docs.title: llm_classifier
docs.text:
Runs one of three judge-backed modes: capability, escalation, or custom. max_output_tokens applies to all three.

Key Required Default Meaning mode No capability Classifier behavior. Set it explicitly for new configurations. classifier_target Capability, escalation — Target the judge is called through. Not a routing destination. Custom mode uses models.judge. max_output_tokens No 4096 Maximum completion tokens for the judge verdict. Must be at least 1. response_format_type No json_schema Structured-output mode for capability and escalation judges. Use json_object when the provider does not support JSON Schema; Switchyard adds the schema to the prompt and validates the verdict locally. Custom mode always uses its configured JSON Schema.

Capability mode classifies before serving. See LLM Classifier Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning strong_target Yes — Capable tier. weak_target Yes — Efficient tier. base_threshold Yes — Lowest solve probability that routes to the weak target. In [0, 1]. fail_open No true Capability mode only. When true, judge client failures and deadlines route to the capable tier and record fail-open evidence. When false, they stop the request. Invalid verdicts use the capable tier with either setting. threshold_step No 0.0 Finite, non-negative amount added once for uncertain or unmatched verdicts and twice for unsupported verdicts. base_threshold + 2 * threshold_step must be at most 1. classify_trigger No every_request When the judge runs. every_request judges every request, tool continuations included. user_turn judges each new user message and retains that target across intervening tool calls only when requests carry a session ID; without a session ID, it behaves like every_request. new_session judges once and reuses that target for the session. message_hash_fallback No false Retains the target against a hash of the first user message when a request carries no session ID. Requires classify_trigger = "new_session" or "user_turn". recent_turn_window No unset When unset, the judge sees the opening task and latest user follow-up, when present. When set, it also sees trailing turns. prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the capability prompt. The packaged schema is sent separately as structured-output configuration.

Escalation mode serves the weak target first and judges the completed turn. See Escalation-Router Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning strong_target Yes — Target used after the session latches. weak_target Yes — Target served before the latch. prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the trajectory-judge prompt. escalation.confirmations No 2 Consecutive fresh-evidence verdicts for the same failure category required to latch. Above 1 needs a stable session ID. escalation.recent_turn_window No 28 Trailing messages shown to the judge. escalation.window_message_chars No 500 Per-message cap inside that window. escalation.deescalation No unset Enables phase-aware de-escalation. Requires a stable session ID. escalation.deescalation.strong_min_calls With de-escalation — Strong-tier turns before release is allowed. Must be at least 1. escalation.deescalation.confirmations With de-escalation — Consecutive judge declines required to return to weak. Must be at least 1. escalation.deescalation.strong_max_calls No unset Hard limit on strong-tier turns before forced de-escalation. Must be at least strong_min_calls. escalation.deescalation.weak_cooldown_calls No 0 Weak calls served without judging after a hard-limit return.

Existing configurations that contain escalation but omit mode remain valid.

Custom mode validates the judge's JSON against response_schema, resolves the policy selector, and routes to a runtime model group. A verdict names a group and the first model in it serves the turn. An eligible non-timeout failure tries the rest of that group, then any remaining models in models.any. A timeout stops the request without trying another model. A connection that times out before it is established counts as a connection failure, not a timeout, so it tries the next model.

The [routes.<name>.models] table takes any group name you choose. any and judge are reserved and required; capable and efficient are reserved for the tier meaning the other algorithms give them. Every other key is yours, which is how one route chooses between more than two models.

Key Required Default Meaning models.any Yes — Every selectable completion target, in fallback order for eligible non-timeout failures. Every other group's targets must also appear here; one that does not is rejected at configuration load. models.judge Yes — One or more ordered judge candidates. The Rust runner calls the first and stops on a client error after retries. Not a completion destination. models.capable No — Ordered capable-tier models. A capable verdict selects the first; eligible non-timeout failures try the rest in order. models.efficient No — Ordered efficient-tier models. An efficient verdict selects the first; eligible non-timeout failures try the rest in order. models.<your name> No — A group you name. A verdict naming it selects its first model; eligible non-timeout failures try the rest in order. default_target Yes — Group used when the judge's verdict cannot be parsed or routed. HTTP client failures stop the request after retries. Any group except judge, and it must contain at least one target. prompt Yes — Judge system prompt. The configured inner schema is sent separately as structured-output configuration. response_schema Yes — Inner JSON Schema encoded as a TOML string. Switchyard adds the provider wrapper. policy Yes — Policy table. target_selector accepts a JSON Pointer such as /decision/target. classify_trigger No every_request When the judge runs. every_request judges every request, tool continuations included. user_turn judges each new user message and retains that target across intervening tool calls only when requests carry a session ID; without a session ID, it behaves like every_request. new_session judges once and reuses that target for the session. message_hash_fallback No false Retains the target against a hash of the first user message when a request carries no session ID. Requires classify_trigger = "new_session" or "user_turn". recent_turn_window No unset When unset, the judge sees the opening task and latest user follow-up, when present. When set, it also sees trailing turns.

The selected JSON label must name a configured group. A label naming a target rather than a group, or a group you did not configure, falls back to default_target. judge is not routable.

Classifier prompts must not contain {{RESPONSE_SCHEMA}}. Switchyard supplies the schema automatically: through the structured-output request in json_schema mode, or in the prompt in json_object mode.

docs.title: stage_router
docs.text:
Scores tool signals to pick a tier per turn. See Stage-Router Routing for how the signals work and for tuning.

Key Required Default Meaning capable_target Yes — Capable tier. efficient_target Yes — Efficient tier. picker Yes — efficient_first, or capable_first (experimental, unbenchmarked). Tier used when the signals are not confident. confidence_threshold Yes — Corroboration a decisive pick needs. In [0, 1]. efficient_first_threshold is accepted as an alias. capable_first_threshold No 0.0 Threshold used after an outer classifier selects the capable tier. Only a composite route sets that tier, so this key has no effect on a standalone stage_router route. recent_turn_window No 3 Trailing tool results the signals are computed over. capable_hold_turns No 2 Requests kept on capable after a switch. Signal-driven capable decisions also start finite holds. Active holds skip signal processing and classification; 0 disables; -1 pins after a switch. efficient_hold_turns No 0 Requests kept on efficient after a switch, even when errors appear. 0 disables; -1 pins after a switch. tool_semantics.observe No [] Exact ASCII case-insensitive domain tool names that count as read-only investigation. tool_semantics.mutate No [] Exact ASCII case-insensitive domain tool names that count as state-changing production. tool_semantics.plan No [] Exact ASCII case-insensitive domain tool names that count as planning or task decomposition. tool_semantics.new No [] Exact ASCII case-insensitive domain tool names that demonstrate forward activity without favoring either tier. handoff_notes No unset Table of notes appended to the forwarded request when the signals pick a tier. Keys below. classifier No unset Table for the optional capability judge consulted on ambiguous turns. Keys below. subagents No unset Nested passthrough or custom llm_classifier policy used only for delegated sub-agent work. See Sub-Agent-Aware Routing.

docs.title: handoff_notes keys
docs.text: Key Required Default Meaning handoff_notes.escalation_note Yes, when the table is present — Note appended to the request when the signals or a hard override escalate to the capable tier. handoff_notes.deescalation_note No unset Note appended to the request whenever the signals select the efficient tier, whether or not a capable turn came before. handoff_notes.only_on_wrong_signal_escalation No true When true, restricts escalation notes to signal-driven capable decisions. Held turns receive no notes with either setting.

docs.title: classifier keys
docs.text:
The judge runs when the signals are ambiguous or the request has no tool history. It runs as a step inside the stage cascade, not as a standalone route, so it is consulted on every ambiguous turn and never retains a verdict.

Key Required Default Meaning classifier.target Yes, when the table is present — Target the judge is called through. Not a routing destination. classifier.base_threshold For LLM judges — Lowest p_solve that still routes to the efficient tier. In [0, 1]. Omit with classifier.decision. classifier.threshold_step No 0.0 Finite, non-negative amount added once for uncertain or unmatched verdicts and twice for unsupported verdicts. base_threshold + 2 * threshold_step must be at most 1. classifier.fail_open No true When true, judge client failures and deadlines let the turn fall open to the picker default and record fail-open evidence. When false, they stop the request. classifier.decision No unset Use a decision model instead of an LLM judge. The classifier target must be in decision_targets. It cannot be combined with base_threshold, threshold_step, prompt, response_format_type, or max_output_tokens; the load error is decision cannot use LLM judge settings. See Decision model classifier. classifier.classify_trigger No every_request Only the default is accepted here. The stage fallback judge runs on every ambiguous turn and retains no verdict, so user_turn and new_session are rejected at load. Use a composite route to judge once per user turn. classifier.message_hash_fallback No false Rejected at load on a stage_router route. The fallback judge retains nothing to key on. classifier.recent_turn_window No unset When unset, the judge sees the opening task and the latest user follow-up. When set, it also sees that many trailing messages. This counts messages, while the route's recent_turn_window counts tool results, so the two values are different units. classifier.prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the capability judge prompt. The verdict schema is unchanged. classifier.response_format_type No json_schema Structured-output mode for the LLM judge. Use json_object when the provider does not support JSON Schema; Switchyard adds the schema to the prompt and validates the verdict locally. Not with classifier.decision. classifier.max_output_tokens No 4096 Maximum completion tokens for the LLM judge verdict. Must be at least 1. Not with classifier.decision.

classifier.response_schema, classifier.policy, and any classifier.mode other than capability are rejected on a stage_router route with custom classifier settings require composite with mode = custom. classifier.mode = "capability" is accepted and changes nothing. Use a composite route for a custom judge.

docs.title: auto
docs.text:
auto is a preset. It builds a stage_router route with fixed settings and no classifier. Use it when you want the recommended starting point without tuning. See Auto for what the preset does and when it does not route.

Key Required Default Meaning capable_target Yes — Capable tier. efficient_target Yes — Efficient tier.

auto accepts no other keys. Adding one is a configuration error. For example, adding confidence_threshold = 0.5 to an auto route fails --dry-run with:

unknown field `confidence_threshold`, expected `capable_target` or `efficient_target`

An auto route behaves the same as this stage_router route. It has no classifier, no handoff notes, and no per-tier system prompts:

[routes.smart]
id = "switchyard"
type = "stage_router"
capable_target = "strong"
efficient_target = "weak"
picker = "efficient_first"
confidence_threshold = 0.5
recent_turn_window = 3
capable_hold_turns = 2

To tune the preset, replace the auto route with this block and edit the keys. The stage_router table lists every key. See Stage-Router Routing for tuning guidance and the model selection guide for choosing the two targets.

docs.title: composite
docs.text:
Composes other algorithms, letting one set another's configuration. Today a classifier selects the stage router's starting tier and confidence threshold. Tool signals still drive escalation and recovery. See Composite Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning classifier.target Yes — Target the tier judge is called through. Not a routing destination. classifier.base_threshold For LLM judges unset p_solve floor that still routes to the efficient tier. In [0, 1]. Omit with classifier.decision. classifier.threshold_step No 0.0 Finite, non-negative amount added once for uncertain or unmatched verdicts and twice for unsupported verdicts. base_threshold + 2 * threshold_step must be at most 1. classifier.classify_trigger Yes — user_turn re-picks the tier whenever the user speaks, new_session picks once and holds it. every_request is rejected here: a judge call per tool step is the cost this route exists to avoid. classifier.decision No unset Use a decision model instead of an LLM judge. The classifier target must be in decision_targets. It cannot be combined with the LLM judge keys (base_threshold, threshold_step, prompt, response_format_type, max_output_tokens). classifier.fail_open No true On judge failure, retain the last classified tier or default to efficient. Set false to return the error. classifier.message_hash_fallback No false Retains the tier by hashing the first user message, for clients that send no session ID. Works with either supported trigger. Conversations opening with the same text share a tier. classifier.recent_turn_window No unset When unset, the judge sees the opening task and latest user follow-up, when present. When set, it also sees trailing turns. classifier.prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the classifier judge prompt. The verdict schema is unchanged. classifier.response_format_type No json_schema Structured-output mode for the judge. Use json_object when the provider does not support JSON Schema. Switchyard adds the schema to the prompt and validates the verdict locally. classifier.max_output_tokens No 4096 Maximum completion tokens for the judge verdict. Must be at least 1. stage.capable_target Yes — Capable tier. stage.efficient_target Yes — Efficient tier. stage.efficient_first_threshold No 0.5 Signal confidence required after an Efficient classification. In [0, 1]. Also accepts confidence_threshold. stage.capable_first_threshold No 0.0 Signal confidence required after a Capable classification. In [0, 1]. stage.recent_turn_window No 3 Trailing tool results the signals are computed over. stage.capable_hold_turns No 2 Same capable hold as stage_router: 0 disables; -1 pins after a switch. stage.efficient_hold_turns No CF: -1; EF: 0 Defaults to pinning efficient after a switch when the classifier selected capable-first. Explicit 0 disables; positive values hold that many requests. stage.tool_semantics.observe No [] Additional exact ASCII case-insensitive tool names that count as observation. stage.tool_semantics.mutate No [] Additional exact ASCII case-insensitive tool names that count as mutation. stage.tool_semantics.plan No [] Additional exact ASCII case-insensitive tool names that count as planning. stage.tool_semantics.new No [] Additional exact ASCII case-insensitive tool names that count as neutral forward activity. stage.handoff_notes No unset Optional guidance appended to forwarded requests. Uses the same fields and behavior as stage-router handoff notes. subagents No unset Nested policy used only for delegated sub-agent work.

For decision classifier configuration, see Decision model classifier. The same decision settings are accepted by the optional stage_router classifier.

The tier is retained per session. A deployment that sends no session ID needs classifier.message_hash_fallback = true, which keys on the first user message instead. The outer [routes.<name>.classifier] table is required. The nested [routes.<name>.stage] table accepts neither picker nor a second classifier. The outer classifier supplies the default tier. A turn the classifier cannot reach falls open to the efficient tier.

docs.title: advisor
docs.text:
Serves every client-visible turn from the executor and has a stronger advisor review terminal turns before the caller sees them: APPROVE releases the buffered turn, REDO discards it and sends the executor back to work with the advisor's plan. See Advisor-Gate Routing.

Key Required Default Meaning executor_target Yes — Serves every client-visible turn. advisor_target Yes — Reviews gated turns. Not a routing destination. gate_trigger No no_tool_call What fires a review: no_tool_call or pattern. gate_trigger_pattern No unset Regex (searched, not anchored) for the pattern trigger. That trigger requires a non-empty pattern; setting one under no_tool_call is rejected. max_reviews No 1 Reviews allowed per session scope. Must be at least 1. gate_stall_turns No 0 Reviews one turn as a mid-task checkpoint once the conversation carries this many assistant turns. 0 disables. gate_min_tool_results No 0 Tool results a conversation needs before a no_tool_call turn is reviewable. advisor_max_tokens No 2048 Maximum output tokens per review. Must be at least 1. advisor_temperature No unset Sampling temperature for reviews. Omitted from the request when unset. transcript_max_chars No 200000 Cap on the transcript sent to the advisor; longer transcripts are trimmed from the middle. Must be at least 256. fail_open No true Lets the gated turn through when the advisor fails, instead of returning an error. reviewer_system_prompt No packaged prompt Replaces the APPROVE/REDO reviewer prompt. redo_feedback_prefix No packaged prompt Replaces the text put in front of a REDO plan fed back to the executor.
